_comment: Example board-language sidecar for the posture section, the shape the ciso-board-translation skill produces. Pass to render_executive.py with --translations. Every figure here is read from examples/example-profile.csfp — the skill supplies structure and judgment, never invented numbers. Keys are optional: omit any and that slot renders as a labelled placeholder. The canonical item key is "gaps"; "subcategories" is a deprecated alias kept readable for older sidecars. See skills/board-pack/references/section-contract.md.
executiveSummary: We set a target of largely-achieved or better across the six outcomes we scoped this cycle, and we are short on five of them. The distance is not evenly spread: two of the five are at zero against a target we chose deliberately, which means the work has not started rather than that it is going slowly. Encryption of data at rest and in transit is the widest single gap and the one a regulator asks about first. Supply-chain risk management is the second, and it is the one that governs how much the other five are worth — controls we hold ourselves to but do not hold a vendor to are controls with a gap in them. Identity and risk-management objectives are both one step short and are the two most likely to close inside the next cycle. We are asking for one decision today: fund the encryption programme, or record that the board accepts data-at-rest exposure for another two quarters.

gaps.PR.DS-01: Data at rest is not encrypted anywhere we have assessed, against a target we set at fully achieved. This is the widest gap in the scope and the one most likely to be asked about first after an incident, because it is the control that decides whether a stolen disk is an inconvenience or a notification.
gaps.GV.SC-01: We have no supply-chain risk management programme, and that governs the worth of every other control here — a standard we hold ourselves to and do not hold a vendor to is a standard with a gap in it.
gaps.GV.RM-01: Risk management objectives are written but not yet agreed with the leadership who own the trade-offs, so the register records our judgement rather than the organisation's.
gaps.PR.AA-01: Identity and credential management is one step short of target: the practice is in place but not applied consistently across services and hardware, which leaves the exceptions as the attack path.
gaps.GV.OC-01: Organisational mission is understood and already informs risk decisions; this is the closest to target and needs consolidation rather than investment.

decisions: Fund the data-at-rest encryption programme to close PR.DS-01, or record the board's acceptance of that exposure for a further two quarters.
Name an owner for supply-chain risk management (GV.SC-01) — the outcome cannot start without one.
